title: Access boundary playbook: hosting deployment matrix and evidence patterns
content:
Purpose and audience:
This playbook is intended for engineering leads (platform, infra, and SRE), security engineers, and compliance owners who need a pragmatic mapping between RBAC role boundaries and the proofs that feed our SIEM / evidence automation system. It complements higher-level IAM guidance by: (1) prescribing role decision criteria per deployment mode (hosted, dedicated, private), (2) listing minimum audit event shapes required for automated evidence collection, and (3) offering lightweight policy templates and enforcement suggestions for rapid adoption.

Scope and assumptions:
- Focus is on operator and tenant-facing privileges (service accounts, admin consoles, tenant owners).
- Not exhaustive for platform internals (e.g., hardware provisioning workflows) but covers the common vectors used during onboarding, deployments, and incident ops.
- We assume log shipping to the central SIEM (Elastic/Chronicle/Splunk) with normalized fields; where agents differ we provide mapping notes.

Role decision matrix (high level):
Note: roles below are recommendations (role names in parentheses). Use principle of least privilege and separation of duties.

1) Hosted (multi-tenant, Redwood-managed control plane)
- Tenant Admin (tenant-admin): manage tenant keys, route configuration, and per-tenant quotas. No host infrastructure privileges.
- Support Engineer (support-readonly, support-ops): read-only access to tenant metadata, request traces, and billing signals. Escalation via ephemeral elevation (just-in-time) with approval ticket.
- Platform Operator (platform-deploy): infra-level deploy rights, node pool management; scoped to tenant tagging when performing tenant-bound operations.

2) Dedicated (customer-dedicated capacity, Redwood-hosted)
- Site Admin (site-admin): full control of capacity pool, model pinning, autoscale policies for the dedicated site. Tenancy isolation required by default.
- Network Admin (net-admin): manage VPC peering/SGs for dedicated pools. Actions logged as platform-level network changes.
- Tenant Operator (tenant-ops-limited): can manage model rollouts and routing rules within assigned dedicated pools; cannot modify platform autoscaler parameters.

3) Private (customer-managed control plane or on-prem)
- Org Admin (org-admin): full control within customer's control plane. Redwood personnel may be granted support roles only via documented support sessions and temporary credentials.
- Support Liaison (support-liaison): read-only unless temporary support sessions are explicitly approved and logged.

Role attributes and enforcement knobs:
- Attributes to attach to roles: assignment scope (tenant, site, org), session duration limit, MFA required, JIT elevation allowed, approved ticket id.
- Enforcement: policy engine checks ticket id presence for any action requiring escalation, and denies if not present. Use short-lived credentials for privileged actions (max 1 hour).

Minimum audit event schema (normalized fields):
We use a normalized shape for evidence automation. If SIEM ingestion uses a different agent, mapping must be declared in the ingestion pipeline. The following field names are required for automated attestation and replay:

Required fields (string unless noted):
- event_id (string)
- timestamp (ISO-8601)
- actor.id (string)  -- unique principal id (service account, user id)
- actor.type (enum) {user, service, system}  -- use lower-case
- actor.identity_provider (string) -- e.g., google-oauth, saml, internal-kms
- action (string) -- canonical action name, e.g., tenant:update-quotas, model:deploy
- resource.id (string) -- resource canonical id (tenant-123, pool-45)
- resource.type (string) -- e.g., tenant, model, pool, kms-key
- outcome (enum) {success, failure, denied}
- auth_context.session_id (string) -- linkable to session traces and ephemeral creds
- request_id (string) -- correlates across services
- ip (string) -- source IP if applicable
- host.agent (string) -- agent/collector id or process name
- raw_payload (string) -- optional JSON blob (retain for forensics)

Optional but recommended:
- justification_ticket (string) -- JIRA/SMC id for JIT approvals
- mfa_asserted (boolean) -- true/false as string 'true'/'false' for normalization
- tenant_quota_change (object as string) -- delta description (keep as stringified JSON)

Notes on shape and implementation: keep fields low-cardinality where possible for SIEM indexing costs; use resource.type and action canonicalization to reduce explosion of unique keys.

Evidence automation contracts (how SIEM pulls proofs):
1) Ticket linkage enforcement
- When a privileged action occurs (action flagged in the policy catalog as privileged), the ingest pipeline validates presence of justification_ticket and session_id. If missing, an enrichment rule flags the event and forwards to the security ops queue.

2) Cross-service correlation rules
- request_id and session_id must be stamped by front-door proxies and passed to downstream services. Correlation playbooks use these to rebuild causal chains for proofs.

3) Snapshot retention and resize proofing
- For actions that alter tenant capacity or model pinning, the evidence pipeline requires two audit points: pre-change snapshot and post-change snapshot. The pipeline will fail automatic approvals if the pre-snapshot is unavailable (retention misconfigured).

SIEM export mapping examples (Elastic ingestion example):
- event_id -> ecs.event.id
- timestamp -> @timestamp
- actor.id -> user.id (if user) or service.id (if service) -- normalize into user.id for our dashboards, set actor.type tag
- action -> event.action
- outcome -> event.outcome
- resource.type -> labels.resource_type

Policy template snippets (YAML-ish, lightweight):
- role: tenant-admin
  scope: tenant
  allow:
    - action: tenant:read*
    - action: tenant:update-quotas
    - condition: requestor.scope == resource.scope
  deny:
    - action: infra:*

- role: support-elevated-temporary
  scope: global
  allow:
    - action: tenant:diagnostics:collect
    - action: tenant:trace:stream
  constraints:
    - max_duration: 01:00:00
    - require: justification_ticket, mfa_asserted

- role: platform-operator
  scope: site
  allow:
    - action: infra:nodepool:*
    - action: infra:autoscaler:set
  constraints:
    - require: approval_ticket

Operational playflows (short):
1) Support JIT elevation (hosted)
- Support engineer opens ticket JIRA-XXXX with tenant, reason, and TTL.
- Approval automation (on-call + manager) executes, stamps justification_ticket.
- Short-lived role is minted with session_id and TTL and logs audit events with justification_ticket.

2) Dedicated pool change (dedicated)
- Site admin proposes autoscale policy change in PR. PR references capacity tests (perf-scan-YYYY).
- Merge triggers pre-change snapshot event (pre-snapshot) and pipeline stores state.
- Autoscaler change applied, post snapshot recorded; evidence automation links pre/post.

3) Remote support to private deployment (private)
- All support sessions require SSO-backed temporary credentials and a recorded support session id.
- If remote runbooks require elevated access, a recorded change window (with explicit consent from customer org-admin) is required. Events tagged with customer-consent: true are accepted by evidence automation.

Risk notes and common pitfalls:
- Missing correlation ids (request_id/session_id) are the most frequent cause of failed evidence artifacts. Instrumentation checklists should be part of any rollout.
- Overly broad resource identifiers increase cardinality and SIEM costs. Prefer typed resource identifiers and add a mapping table for human-friendly names.
- Inconsistent justification_ticket formats (free text vs. structured id) break automated linking. Use a templated ticket creation step in runbooks.

Checklist for rollout (minimum viable automation):
- [ ] Canonicalize action names and resource.type enum
- [ ] Ensure front-door proxies set request_id and session_id on inbound traffic
- [ ] Add event enrichment to insert justification_ticket validation for privileged actions
- [ ] Build two snapshot hooks for capacity/pinning changes
- [ ] Create SIEM dashboards showing missing-justification events and pre/post snapshot mismatches

Appendix: quick grep-ready audit filters and SIEM queries (examples)
- Missing justification (Elasticsearch KQL): NOT justification_ticket:* AND event.action:("tenant:update-quotas" OR "infra:autoscaler:set")
- Pre/post mismatch detection (pseudo SQL): SELECT request_id FROM events WHERE action IN ("pre-snapshot", "post-snapshot") GROUP BY request_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT action) < 2

Next steps and owning teams:
- Instrumentation: infra/observability (Marcus Liu) to add request/session stamping and enrichment.
- Policy engine changes: eng-platform (Priya Verma) to add constraint evaluation for justification_ticket and TF for short-lived role minting.
- SIEM automation: security-ops (Eva Schultz) to onboard dashboards and playbooks for missing evidence alerts.

Open questions for review:
- Should we add cryptographic signing of pre/post snapshots for higher assurance? Tradeoff: additional complexity and storage.
- What TTL for elevated support roles is acceptable for enterprise customers vs. standard hosted customers?
